title: Retention & redaction prioritization lattice with risk-adjusted intake slots
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Define and build an operational prioritization lattice for customer requests related to log retention, PII redaction, and audit export needs. This ticket delivers a risk-adjusted intake model that maps incoming requests to deterministic response paths and SLOs, enabling consistent customer communications and predictable engineering commitments. We want to reduce time-to-resolution for high-risk enterprise requests while automating safe declines or self-serve guidance for low-risk asks.
background: We receive varied enterprise requests (retention extensions, selective redaction, export for audits) with inconsistent routing. Current ad-hoc handling creates long tails, missed SLAs, and unclear engineering scope. Existing playbooks focus on triage heuristics but lack a single scored lattice that combines privacy risk, customer tier, engineering effort, and regulatory urgency into routing slots. This proposal introduces 'risk-adjusted slots' — four deterministic outcomes with documented SLOs and handoffs.
scoring_components: PII sensitivity (0-5), System exposure (0-5), Regulatory urgency (0-5), Business criticality / contract obligation (0-5), Engineering implementation complexity estimate (0-5). Each component has guidance and examples in the companion scoring rubric. We normalize and weight scores to produce a 0-100 risk score. Weights proposed: PII 30%, Reg 25%, Exposure 20%, Business 15%, Complexity 10%.
routing_slots: Slot A (Immediate escalation): score >= 75 -> SLA: 24h ack, 7d assessment, 30d resolution target or agreed carve-out. Trigger: legal/regulatory requirement, contractual SLA breach risk, or customer-data-exfiltration exposure. Slot B (High priority triage): 50-74 -> SLA: 24h ack, 3 business day initial plan, prioritized engineering backlog within sprint. Slot C (Standard backlog): 25-49 -> SLA: 48h ack, assessment within 2 weeks, grouped into monthly governance sprint. Slot D (Self-serve / Docs or decline): <25 -> Provide template guidance, recommended self-serve steps, or decline with remediation suggestions and product feature suggestions for product team consideration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Documented scoring rubric with examples for 10 common request types (retention change, selective redaction, export frequency, deletion requests, ephemeral logging). 2) Decision matrix mapping score ranges to routing slots and required handoffs (Legal, Security, Engineering, CS). 3) Automated intake form prototype that computes risk score and suggests slot. 4) Response templates for each slot with SLA commitments. 5) A runbook for escalation to Slot A with on-call contacts and legal notice templates.
implementation_tasks: - Finalize scoring rubric and weights with Privacy and Legal. - Build intake form (Zendesk/ServiceNow/Hub) fields to capture scoring components. - Add computed score to request metadata and display in Intake dashboard. - Implement routing automation to create either ENG or CS tasks and Slack alerts for Slot A. - Write response templates and CS playbook. - Add telemetry to measure flow times by slot and report weekly.
out_of_scope: Ad-hoc engineering changes for per-customer custom pipelines. Full enforcement tooling (e.g., automatic redaction engine) is out of scope; this ticket focuses on intake, prioritization and routing only.
risk_mitigation: Start with a conservative scoring calibration and pilot with 2 enterprise customers. Maintain human-in-loop for all Slot A decisions for first 6 weeks. Legal to review all Slot A assessments prior to customer-facing commitments.
metrics_and_success: Primary metrics: median time-to-initial-assessment, % of requests meeting slot SLOs, reduction in escalations due to missed SLAs, CS satisfaction score for governance requests. Success target: 90% of Slot A requests get initial assessment within 7 days and overall triage SLOs improve by 40% in pilot cohort.
